market_summary: Canadian banks were mixed on Aug 29 despite a blockbuster Q3 earnings week: TD +1.19% led on a 26% adjusted EPS beat, while CM –2.85%, RY –1.61% and ZEB –0.80% gave back post-earnings gains. XFN and ZWB also slipped, with only the TSX Composite marginally positive (+0.06%), signaling profit-taking after all six lenders beat Bay Street estimates on capital-markets strength.

top_story.headline: CMHC: Ontario Mortgage Delinquencies Pass National Average for First Time Since 2012 — Toronto +60% YoY to 0.24%
top_story.why_it_matters: Ontario crossing above the 0.22% national average marks a regime shift in housing credit risk concentrated in Toronto condos. Even though Big Six losses remain low on ~58% LTV cushions, the 45% YoY jump in Toronto delinquency and CIBC/BMO 0.51–0.56% readings mean provisions on performing loans will stay elevated and OSFI will keep CET1 buffers (RBC 13.5%, BMO 13.0%) tight into renewal season.

themes.title: Q3 Earnings Beat — But Provisions Creep Higher
themes.synthesis: All Big Six beat on pre-provision, pre-tax earnings (RBC $8.7B +13%, CIBC $3.96B +20%), but PCL ratios ticked to 36–56 bps (RBC 36 bps, Scotia 56 bps, BMO 41 bps) with performing-loan provisions returning.

themes.title: Ontario Housing Stress Concentrates — National Average Misleads
themes.synthesis: National 90+ day rate actually dipped to 0.22% in Q2 2025, but Ontario rose to 0.23–0.41% (balance-level) and Toronto condos drive the increase as investors with 2021 peak-price, low-equity loans face renewal shocks.

themes.title: Losses Contained, but LTV and PCL Trajectory Matters
themes.synthesis: Banks flag low realized losses thanks to 54–62% GTA LTVs, yet CIBC GTA LTV rose to 62% from 56% and BMO impaired-mortgage PCL doubled to 7 bps annualized, so the next two quarters of renewals will test reserves.

themes.title: NIM Expansion & Capital Return — Positive Offset Not in Cluster
themes.synthesis: Q3 NIM ex-trading 2.07% (+12 bps yoy at BMO) and $420M ZEB inflows on dividend resilience plus BMO's pending $25M NCIB show capital return is the positive driver the clustering missed this week — NIM > PCL is why the thesis is Watch not Breaking despite delinquency breach.

outlook: Watch OSFI guidance on capital return (BMO new $25M share NCIB pending) and September Canadian housing/Teranet plus Bank of Canada commentary on renewal cliff — if Ontario delinquency holds above national into Q4, expect banks to keep provisioning skewed to performing loans.
